raw_plan.interpretation: A single acquisition email for the selected technical-founder audience, written at audience level because no individual company has been qualified. The email will earn a low-friction product evaluation by inviting the reader to inspect Fathom’s live dashboard before starting a trial or changing their analytics setup.

intent.desired_action: View Fathom’s live dashboard and decide whether its single-page view is sufficient for the reader’s routine website traffic questions.

raw_plan.reader: A technical founder or small-team operator who maintains their own web properties and wants essential traffic information without navigating a complex analytics interface.
raw_plan.reader_segment: A technical founder who built the site himself and gave up on GA4 somewhere around the third Explore report
raw_plan.reader_scope: Address founders who personally review traffic on sites they maintain. Do not imply that any specific recipient currently uses GA4, has attempted a migration, runs a consent banner, or has been individually qualified.
raw_plan.promise: The reader can inspect whether Fathom’s single-page dashboard gives them the website view they need before changing their current setup.
raw_plan.orientation: Fathom is a hosted, cookieless website analytics dashboard that technical founders can add to a site and read on a single page, on a paid plan rather than a free tier.
raw_plan.arc: Move the reader from recognizing the familiar burden of digging through an analytics interface to seeing a concrete, no-installation way to judge a simpler one-page alternative.
raw_plan.sequence_rationale: With only one email, the argument must contain the problem, documented product mechanism, and evaluation step in one self-contained progression. Dashboard simplicity leads because it directly addresses verified problem P1 and can be inspected through a clickable live dashboard without assuming an installed tool or requiring deployment. The no-cookie argument remains a complete alternative proposition because it addresses a different verified problem but requires a higher-friction trial to test on the reader’s own site.

emails.selection_reason: The selected reader wants basic website information without a buried interface. Fathom’s documented single-page dashboard directly addresses that need, and the live dashboard lets an unqualified prospect inspect the interface before committing to a trial or installation.
emails.target_audience: Technical founders and small-team operators who personally maintain their sites and find conventional analytics interfaces more complex than the traffic questions they need answered.
emails.job: Get the reader to inspect the live dashboard and decide whether Fathom’s one-page analytics view merits an evaluation on their own site.
emails.single_idea: You do not have to switch analytics to find out whether Fathom is simpler: its live demo shows the single-page dashboard before you install anything.
emails.felt_need: I want to see what is happening on my site without digging through layers of reports I do not need.
emails.status_quo: Technical founders commonly start with Google Analytics and some later look for privacy-focused alternatives when its interface becomes difficult to navigate for basic traffic questions.
emails.why_it_fails: For this audience, the conventional interface can bury the basic information they want inside more complexity than a self-managed site requires.
emails.mechanism: Fathom presents its analytics on one filterable page. A clickable live dashboard lets the reader inspect that layout directly, including whether the available view is sufficient for their routine traffic review, without first installing the product.

If finding basic website information means navigating more reports than you need, the layout may be worth a look. It brings the core view together without requiring months of training.

The clickable dashboard shows how that view handles live visitors, pageviews, top pages, referrers, countries, devices, browsers, events and UTM campaigns.

You can explore the interface without creating an account or changing your current analytics setup, then decide whether it merits a trial on your own site.
